requirement: API-first: Every capability available in the UI is available via API. The UI is a client of the same contracts.
CBA-agnostic core: No CBA-specific field, code, or behaviour appears outside an adapter. Enforced by architectural test.
Configuration over code: Tenant differences are data. Tenant-specific code is a last resort and must be isolated in extension points.
Event-sourced state transitions: Application state changes are recorded as immutable events; current state is a projection. Underpins audit and replay.
Idempotency everywhere: Every external-effect operation carries an idempotency key. Retries are safe by design.
Explainable decisioning: Any automated decision stores its inputs, policy version, model version, and reason codes.
Least privilege by default: New roles start with zero permissions. Access is granted, never assumed.
Fail visible, not silent: Integration failures create actionable exceptions in a queue; they never silently degrade a decision.
Data minimization: Collect what policy requires. PII access is logged and purpose-bound.
Deployment neutrality: One artefact runs SaaS, private cloud, and on-premise. No hosting-model-specific code paths.
Deployable on-premise, in private cloud and as multi-tenant SaaS from one codebase (data residency driver).
Some tenants require air-gapped or restricted-egress deployment; core paths must not depend on external SaaS.
Maintain a traceability matrix: driver → epic/story → acceptance criteria → test → regulatory citation; no requirement reaches done without a mapped test.
Support multiple tenants (banks) on one deployment with complete logical data isolation; no query path may return cross-tenant data
notes: Defence in depth: app tenant scoping + PostgreSQL RLS (G-18). Test: architectural + cross-tenant pen suite (G-42).
